judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's mathematical claims are all correct and I confirmed each independently: i^5 = i and i^27 = i^3 = -i; (3+2i) + (-1+4i) = 2+6i; i(3+4i) = -4+3i, which is the (3,4) to (-4,3) quarter turn the judge cites; |3+4i| = 5; x^2 + 9 = 0 gives plus/minus 3i; 3i^15 - 2i^22 = -3i + 2 = 2 - 3i; i^4(1+2i) = 1+2i; x^4 - 16 = (x-2)(x+2)(x^2+4) gives 2, -2, 2i, -2i; and x^2 - 4x + 13 = 0 gives 2 plus/minus 3i. All eight study-guide items check too. But the judge scored instruction_following 4/4 without testing the prompt's explicit clause 'clearly label any genuinely open response for manual review', and this sheet fails it plainly. final_response.md asserts 'Nothing on this sheet is open-ended, so nothing is flagged manual' while six of the ten problems end in an explicit written question and three require a drawn representation on a supplied Re/Im grid; gate_log.txt reports '10 passed - 0 failed - 0 manual'. Separately, final_response.md claims 'references/standards-map.md has no complex-number code'; the map has two rows of them at lines 115-116, including the more specific HSN-CN.A.1-A.3 that this sheet's plane work actually exercises.

strengths_to_preserve: The sheet earns the concept-models brief instead of decorating a computation sheet with grids. Problem 1 makes the student DISCOVER the four-cycle from a partly filled table rather than announcing it; problem 4 makes i(3+4i) = -4+3i visibly a quarter turn on its own plane; and problem 8 asks why four quarter turns must return you to the start BEFORE any arithmetic is done. The geometric fact and the algebraic fact are introduced as the same fact.

Problem 5 recovers the modulus by dropping a right triangle from (3,4) to the real axis, so |3+4i| = 5 arrives as the Pythagorean theorem the student already owns rather than as a new formula; the key names it ('This distance is called the modulus') only after it has been derived.

"domain": "complex" is set on the solve and zeros items (6, 9, 10), so the verifier REQUIRES the non-real roots rather than silently accepting a real-only answer set. That is the correct verification posture for a complex-numbers sheet.

The answer key ties problems 4, 8, 9 and 10 back to the cycle established in problem 1, so the sheet reads as one argument: multiplying by i is a quarter turn, four quarter turns is the identity, and that is why i^4 = 1.

root_causes.description: Every problem was recorded as machine-verified because each contains one computable value, but most of them also print a written or drawn response slot that no entry covers. With zero manual entries the build exits 0 and the delivered response tells the reader there is nothing for a human to grade - on a sheet whose whole design is 'a picture or a pattern AND the notation that records it'.
evidence: Worksheet directions: 'Every problem below has two halves: a picture or a pattern and the notation that records it. Do both.'

Problem 1 also asks 'What is i^5, and why does the table start repeating there?'; problem 4 'Describe in one sentence what multiplying by i did to the arrow'; problem 6 'say where the two solutions sit on the complex plane and what the picture has to do with the fact that the parabola never crosses the x-axis'; problem 8 'explain why the picture guarantees that answer'; problem 9 'Say which zeros are real and which are not, and describe the pattern the four points make'; problem 10 'Explain why that mirror symmetry has to happen for any quadratic with real coefficients'.
Problems 3, 4 and 5 each supply a blank Re/Im grid and require plotting - a drawn representation, which is on the canonical open-response list.

verify.json contains ten entries, all typed eval/solve/zeros; gate_log.txt step 5 reports '10 passed - 0 failed - 0 manual'; final_response.md: 'Nothing on this sheet is open-ended, so nothing is flagged manual.'

root_causes.description: Problem 1 prints three empty table cells and verifies one of them. The stem says 'Fill in the three empty cells' - i^3, i^4 and i^5 - and verify.json id 1 checks only i^5, so i^3 = -i and i^4 = 1 are printed answer slots with no recorded expected value.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 1: a table with headers i^1 through i^5, values i and -1 supplied, three cells blank, captioned 'Fill in the three empty cells'.
answer_key.pdf problem 1 supplies all three ('i^3 = i^2 . i = -i, i^4 = (i^2)^2 = 1, and i^5 = i^4 . i = i'), so the key knows about slots the verifier does not.

root_causes.description: SKILL.md tells the author to take standards codes from references/standards-map.md and never to invent one, but it never says to SEARCH that file for the standard the request actually names. The result is a silent nearest-neighbour substitution plus a delivered claim that the map lacks the code - and the map's header explicitly warns against exactly this ("say so rather than reaching for the nearest one"). No gate inspects the tag, so the substitution passes every check.
evidence: final_response.md: 'references/standards-map.md has no complex-number code, so the complex-plane problems carry the task's own HSN-CN reference'.

references/standards-map.md line 115: '| Complex numbers: arithmetic & the complex plane | HSN-CN.A.1-A.3, HSN-CN.B.4-B.6 |'; line 116: '| Complex solutions of polynomials | HSN-CN.C.7-C.9 |'. The first row's title is this sheet's topic verbatim.
As a result seven problems carry the bare family code 'HSN-CN' rather than the specific in-map codes, and problems 6, 9 and 10 could have carried HSN-CN.C.7-C.9.

improvements.title: Any problem whose stem asks the student to explain, diagnose, name an error, or draw a representation must carry a manual verify entry
improvements.proposed_change: Add a rule to SKILL.md and a lint to the gate chain. Rule: a problem is machine-verified only for the quantities it computes; if its stem also carries an open-response imperative (explain, describe, justify, state why, say what/which/why, name the mistake, compare and state, plot, sketch, draw, label, complete the table) the verify JSON must carry an additional {"type": "manual"} entry under the same id describing what the written or drawn answer must contain. curr-334's verify.json in this same run is the working model - it pairs a machine entry per computed quantity with a manual entry per written diagnosis. Lint: scripts/verify.py already segments the worksheet .tex per problem for the prose-consistency gate; reuse that segmentation to scan each stem for the imperative list and fail when a matching problem has no manual entry.
improvements.regression_test: New fixture pairing curr-351's worksheet problem 4 stem ("Plot 3 + 4i. Then compute i(3+4i) ... and plot it too. Describe in one sentence what multiplying by i did to the arrow.") with a verify JSON holding only {"id": 4, "type": "eval", "expected": "-4 + 3*I"}. The lint must fail, naming problem 4 and the triggering words 'Plot' and 'Describe'. Today that exact pair builds green and reports '10 passed - 0 failed - 0 manual'.
improvements.expected_impact: Stops the delivered response claiming 'nothing on this sheet is open-ended' about sheets that are mostly open-ended, and restores the prompt's explicit requirement to label genuinely open responses for manual review. A grader currently receives a green build and no signal that half the sheet needs a human.
improvements.risk: Medium. A keyword scan over-fires on stems that say 'describe your method' as advice rather than as a graded slot, and on 'state the units' where the unit is already bound by answer_unit. Mitigate by keeping the imperative list short and explicit and by letting an author suppress a hit with an explicit "open_response": false marker on the problem, which is auditable.

improvements.title: One verify entry per printed response slot, including enumerated sub-parts and trailing second questions
improvements.proposed_change: Require the verify JSON to carry as many entries under an id as the printed problem has response slots. Sub-parts written as (a)/(b)/(c), and trailing extra questions ('Then check: what is m<A?', 'State how many zeros the theorem supplied'), each need their own entry - machine-typed where a value is computable, manual where it is not. Add a lint that, per problem segment of the worksheet .tex, counts enumerated \item sub-parts and \ansline / \answerline occurrences and fails when that count exceeds the number of verify entries sharing the id. curr-334 already satisfies this and should be cited in SKILL.md as the pattern to copy.
improvements.regression_test: New fixture from curr-301 problem 4: a stem enumerating (a) write the converse, (b) compute QR, (c) explain why PQRS makes the converse false, paired with the single verify entry {"id": 4, "type": "distance", "expected": 3}. The lint must fail with 'problem 4: 3 printed slots, 1 verify entry'. The current tree passes this fixture - it is what shipped.
improvements.expected_impact: Closes the largest verification blind spot in the shard: sheets that read as fully verified while a third of what the student writes is unrecorded, and answer keys whose Quick Answers bank prints one value for a two-answer question.
improvements.risk: Low-medium. The \item count is a heuristic: a sub-part that is pure scaffolding ('redraw the two triangles separately first') is not a response slot and would false-positive. Let the author mark such an item so the exclusion is auditable rather than silent.

improvements.title: Search references/standards-map.md for the requested code family before substituting a different standard, and never assert the map lacks a code without searching
improvements.proposed_change: Two changes. (1) SKILL.md's tagging paragraph currently says only "a code from references/standards-map.md - never invent codes". Add the missing first step: before writing any "standard" value, do a literal substring search of references/standards-map.md for the code family the request names (HSG-CO, HSG-GMD, HSG-MG, HSN-CN, HSN-RN, HSA-REI.A, ...) and for the topic words, and use the matching row's code. Only when that search genuinely returns nothing may the sheet deviate, and the map's own header rule then applies verbatim: "say so rather than reaching for the nearest one", plus add the real row in the same change. Forbid stating in final_response.md that a code is absent from the map unless that search was actually run. (2) Add a band-consistency lint to scripts/verify.py: compare each problem's "standard" prefix with the course level the answer key declares and fail the build when a High-School sheet is tagged with a K-8 code (8.G, 7.EE, 6.EE, ...), printing the high-school rows of the map as the alternatives.
improvements.regression_test: New fixture tests/fixtures/standards_band_mismatch/: a verify JSON whose ten problems are all tagged "8.G.C.9", paired with an answer key whose declared level is "High School Geometry - Modeling with Measurement". scripts/verify.py must exit non-zero and name HSG-GMD.A.1-A.3 / HSG-MG.A.1-A.3 from the map. Run against the current tree the fixture passes silently, which is exactly how curr-345 shipped with a fully green gate chain.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes a demonstrably false statement about the repository's own reference file from delivered responses, and puts the contracted standard back on the answer key's Curriculum block - the one line a parent or teacher reads to place the sheet in a course. Six of the ten cases in this shard are affected.
improvements.risk: Low. The lint is additive and fires only on a grade-prefix/course mismatch. The care point is band vocabulary: an Algebra 2 or Pre-Algebra sheet can legitimately carry an 8.EE-style code for review material, so the lint should warn rather than fail when the course string is a middle-school or transitional course.

case_summary: Mathematically flawless - all ten worksheet answers and all eight study-guide answers verify independently, and the concept-model design (discover the cycle, see multiplication by i as a quarter turn, recover the modulus from a right triangle) is genuinely good teaching. The defect is the verification posture. Six problems end in an explicit 'explain / describe / say why' question and three require plotting on a supplied grid, yet verify.json contains zero manual entries, the build exits 0, and final_response.md states 'Nothing on this sheet is open-ended'. Problem 1 additionally prints three blank table cells and verifies one. A third issue: final_response.md claims the standards map has no complex-number code when it carries two such rows at lines 115-116. The mathematics justifies the ACCEPT; the instruction-following score does not survive contact with the prompt's manual-review clause.
